title: A Witness for the Will
premise: Sable Eriksen, coroner of the fog-bound town of Marrow Bay, is hired by a nervous stranger who pays triple to prove that a murder will not happen at the upcoming Harrow family anniversary dinner — a murder Sable realizes matches, in every detail, an unsolved death from thirty years ago. As Sable digs into old alibis and the town's carefully buried history, they discover the stranger is the presumed-dead heir of the Harrow family, living under a false identity, and that the 'future murder' is a rehearsed repetition someone intends to complete. At the anniversary dinner, Sable must choose between exposing the truth through legal channels — which would destroy the heir's new life and the love growing between them — or letting justice happen outside the law; in the end, Sable engineers a confession by staging the past death's evidence at the dinner table, the true killer (the family patriarch) is arrested on thirty-year-old charges, and the heir walks free into a new name and a life with Sable.
about_author: Bram Montrose is the pen name of a former small-town court clerk who spent a decade transcribing testimony in coastal communities where everyone knew everyone's business. They write mysteries about the quiet violence of towns that keep their own records.

chapters.title: The Client Who Paid for Nothing
chapters.summary: Sable Eriksen's POV. A stranger named Wren arrives at the coroner's office with an envelope of cash, asking Sable to prove a murder will not occur at the Harrow anniversary dinner in three weeks. Sable, pragmatic and bored, takes the retainer as easy money. Emotional beat: wary curiosity masked by professional detachment.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Establishing Marrow Bay: the cemetery rows Sable tends, the filing cabinets of unsolved cases, the town's polite silence. Sable pulls the file on Lorna Harrow, dead thirty years ago this month, ruled accidental drowning. The details of Wren's predicted murder match it exactly. Beat: unease taking root.

chapters.title: Alibis in Amber
chapters.summary: Sable interviews the surviving Harrows under pretext of updating records. Patriarch Edmund Harrow is charming and iron-fisted; his daughter Vivienne is brittle; son Aldous drinks. Each recites the same thirty-year-old alibi word for word — too word for word. Beat: the sense of a script being performed.

chapters.title: What the Water Kept
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren watches the Harrow house from the bluffs, revealing fragments of intimate knowledge of its rooms. Wren meets Sable secretly and insists the murder can be prevented only if no one learns Wren's identity. Beat: fear braided with longing for a home Wren cannot enter.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Guest List
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The dinner invitation list surfaces: twelve guests, one extra place setting already laid for a guest who hasn't confirmed. Sable cross-references it against the thirty-year-old dinner party held the night Lorna died. Same seats, same menu. Beat: ritual horror.

chapters.title: Drowned Twice
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, with flashback texture. Exhumation paperwork stalls — Edmund blocks it through the town council. Sable turns to the original autopsy notes and finds Sable's own predecessor falsified the drowning findings: Lorna had defensive bruises. Beat: righteous anger; the law itself was complicit.

chapters.title: A Love That Files Itself Under Later
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Sable and Wren work late over the case files; attraction sharpens into something neither names. Wren nearly reveals a secret, stops. Sable notices Wren's hands know the Harrow piano. Beat: tenderness complicated by suspicion.

chapters.title: Vivienne Breaks Pattern
chapters.summary: Vivienne's POV. Vivienne, who has repeated her alibi for thirty years, privately tells Sable she remembers a fourth person at the dock that night — someone the family paid to forget. She begs Sable to stop digging before the dinner. Beat: terror wearing the mask of caution.

chapters.title: The Heir Who Drowned
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Records search reveals Lorna's child, Rowan Harrow, officially drowned at sea eight years after her death — but the body was never found. Sable confronts Wren with the photograph. Wren admits it: Rowan survived, was hidden away, raised under another name. Beat: betrayal and revelation colliding.

chapters.title: Why Prove a Negative
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren explains: letters from an anonymous sender have promised for months that Lorna's murder will be re-enacted at the anniversary dinner, with Rowan named as the next victim unless the past is proven first. Wren hired Sable not to solve the crime but to prevent becoming its victim. Beat: dread reframed — Sable isn't solving a mystery, they're standing in one.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Word-for-Word
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable maps the identical alibis and realizes they were coordinated by the family lawyer, Corliss, who drafted them the morning after Lorna died. Corliss, now dying, hints that Edmund gave the order — but dies before signing a statement. Beat: hope extinguished; the legal road closes.

chapters.title: The Extra Place Setting
chapters.summary: Aldous's POV. Drunk and unraveling, Aldous confesses he saw his father at the dock that night and has been bought with allowance and fear ever since. He warns Sable the anonymous letter-writer is someone inside the house. Beat: self-loathing cracking into courage.

chapters.title: Staying Invisible Was Never an Option
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable realizes investigating has made both Sable and Wren targets; Sable's office is searched, files photographed. The sheriff — Edmund's old friend — offers Sable a promotion to look away. Beat: isolation; the cost of seeing clearly.

chapters.title: Letters in Lorna's Hand
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren decodes the anonymous letters' phrasing and recognizes their mother's private idioms — impossible, unless someone kept her papers and speaks in her voice. Suspicion falls on the household cook, Marta, Lorna's only confidante. Beat: grief weaponized into detection.

chapters.title: Marta's Testimony
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Marta admits she wrote the letters: she witnessed Edmund drown Lorna, was silenced for thirty years, and sent them to force the truth before she dies. But she never intended harm to Rowan — someone altered her letters. A third hand is in the game. Beat: relief curdling into new fear.

chapters.title: The Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Surveillance of the house reveals the staff rehearsing the dinner — including a locked boathouse prepared exactly as the dock was thirty years ago. Someone is staging the scene regardless of whether anyone dies. Beat: escalating menace; the trap has two victims designed into it.

chapters.title: Anniversary Eve
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. On the eve of the dinner, Wren decides to attend openly as Rowan, forcing the killer's hand. Sable objects — duty says call the sheriff, love says stand beside them. They choose each other and walk in together. Beat: love against duty, decided.

chapters.title: The Toast
chapters.summary: Rowan/Wren's POV. At the dinner, Rowan rises during Edmund's toast and announces themselves. The room fractures; Edmund's composure holds just long enough to signal someone else — Vivienne, whose brittle calm finally makes sense. Beat: public unmasking, private horror.

chapters.title: Two Killers, One Dock
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Climax at the boathouse: Vivienne, not Edmund, plans to kill Rowan — she helped her father thirty years ago and cannot let the witness live. Edmund, confronted with Sable's staged recreation of Lorna's evidence, breaks and confesses to save himself, implicating Vivienne. Sheriff's deputies arrive; the law finally moves. Beat: violent climax, justice arriving sideways.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Aftermath: Edmund and Vivienne charged with Lorna's murder; the town reels as its alphabetized secrets spill into open court. Sable reflects that the confession would never have come through procedure alone — it took a forged grave, a staged dinner, and a lie told in service of truth. Beat: moral reckoning, earned peace.

chapters.title: A New Name, Filed Under Home
chapters.summary: Rowan's POV. Rowan legally sheds the false identity and chooses a new name — not Harrow. They visit Lorna's grave with Sable, reading the corrected headstone inscription aloud. Beat: grief transformed into inheritance of a gentler kind.

chapters.title: The Next Client
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Months later, a new stranger enters the coroner's office with an envelope of cash and an impossible request. Sable glances at Rowan waiting outside, then opens the file anyway. Final beat: the cycle continues, but this time Sable doesn't face it invisible — or alone.
